repo_notes.content: N1904addons is a Text-Fabric feature extension for the Nestle 1904 Greek New Testament (CenterBLC/N1904). It adds >1,000 features focused on Morpheus morphological analyses, statistical measures of ambiguity and diversity, cross-references, and utility annotations. Features are released under CC BY 4.0 and are marked stable or experimental. Primary author: Tony Jurg (VU Amsterdam). Related thesis: 'Visualising Overlooked Morphosyntactic Alternatives' (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17086524).

pages.title: Overview of N1904addons
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to the project: purpose, relationship to the base N1904-TF dataset, feature maturity flags (stable vs experimental), feature group summary, and how this wiki is organised. Links to Getting Started, Feature Groups, and Use Cases.

page_notes.content: Emphasise that the repository continues to grow and that all features are provided 'as is'. Mention the GitHub repo, Zenodo DOI, and thesis connection.

pages.title: About Text-Fabric
pages.purpose: Brief explanation of Text-Fabric as a graph-based framework (nodes, edges, features) for ancient-language corpora, its modular .tf file design, and why it is particularly suitable for adding morphological and statistical annotations.

page_notes.content: Point users to the official Text-Fabric documentation and the N1904 tutorial for first-time users.

pages.title: Getting Started: Loading the Dataset
pages.purpose: Complete step-by-step guide: install Text-Fabric (including GitHub support), import the use function, load the standard N1904addons feature set via mod=, optionally load the detailed_set, handle GitHub API rate limits with a personal access token, and common error messages.

page_notes.content: Include the exact use() call patterns shown in the documentation and the PDF. Note that the detailed Morpheus md* features are deliberately not loaded by default because of their size.

pages.title: Repository Structure and Versioning
pages.purpose: Describe the physical layout: tf/1.0.0/ (standard features), detailed_set/1.0.0/ (md* block-level features), docs/, and the versioning scheme used by Text-Fabric. Explain the two-module loading pattern.

page_notes.content: Clarify that standard features load with mod="tonyjurg/N1904addons/tf/" while the detailed set requires an additional path in the mod list.

pages.title: Feature Groups Overview
pages.purpose: Map of the four main functional groups (Morpheus, Statistical, Cross-reference, Miscellaneous) and the optional detailed Morpheus set. Indicates which groups are loaded by default.

page_notes.content: Use the exact grouping and short descriptions from the PDF and docs/README.md.

pages.title: Morpheus Feature System
pages.purpose: Architectural overview of the four Morpheus layers (Meta mm_*, Summary ms{ind}_*, Detail md{ind}_*, Analytic ma{ind}_*) and the hierarchical drill-down workflow. Introduces the naming conventions and the relationship between layers.

page_notes.content: Include the conceptual diagram description (meta → summary → detail) and the rationale for the layered design (memory efficiency + progressive disclosure of ambiguity).

pages.title: Meta Features (mm_*)
pages.purpose: Reference for all word-level meta features: mm_num_lemmas, mm_num_blocks, mm_num_morphs, mm_max_sim, mm_raw_uc, mm_raw_bc, mm_gram_dif. Data types, node type, meaning, and typical values.

page_notes.content: These features give a quick per-word overview of how many analyses Morpheus returned and how similar the best one is to the N1904-TF tagging.

pages.title: Summary Features (ms{ind}_*)
pages.purpose: Reference for lemma-grouped summary features indexed by {ind}. Covers lemma forms (base/full, Unicode/Beta Code), homonym and plural-suffix markers, morph tags, morph similarity, block numbers, and gram_dif.

page_notes.content: Explain the grouping-by-lemma concept and how ms{ind}_block_nums links a summary group to the underlying detail blocks.

pages.title: Detail Features (md{ind}_*) and the detailed_set
pages.purpose: Description of the large set of block-level features (md{ind}_{inf_elem}) that expose virtually every element of a Morpheus analytic block. Loading requirements, memory considerations, and the naming pattern.

page_notes.content: These features are stored in detailed_set/1.0.0/ and must be requested explicitly. They are intended for advanced exploration rather than routine use.

pages.title: Analytic Features (ma{ind}_*)
pages.purpose: Phrase-level features derived from comparing Morpheus analyses with N1904-TF syntax, focusing on phrase-function alternatives and flip potential (ma{ind}_pf_altern, ma{ind}_pf_flip, ma_pf_max_flip).

page_notes.content: Highlight the research goal of quantifying how morphological ambiguity can affect syntactic interpretation at the phrase level.

pages.title: The gram_dif Field Map
pages.purpose: Detailed explanation of the 9-character grammatical difference string used across mm_, ms_, and md_ features. Character positions (lemma, person, case, number, gender, tense, mood, voice, degree), agreement/disagreement coding, and practical querying patterns.

page_notes.content: This is one of the most frequently used diagnostic features for spotting morphological mismatches.

pages.title: Statistical Features
pages.purpose: Overview of pre-computed statistical measures: Shannon entropy (absolute and normalised), Type-to-Token Ratios, TF-IDF scores, and word counts. Common design patterns (integer scaling, node-type scope).

page_notes.content: These features support quantitative study of morphological and lexical diversity and of how surface forms, lemmas, and morph tags predict phrase function.

pages.title: Shannon Entropy Features
pages.purpose: Full reference for lemma_entr_mbit/norm, morph_entr_mbit/norm, and text_entr_mbit/norm. Mathematical background, scaling to millibits and 0–1000 range, and interpretation as predictors of parent phrase function.

page_notes.content: Explain the 11 phrase-function classes used in the underlying probability models.

pages.title: Type-to-Token Ratio Features
pages.purpose: Reference for lemma_ttr, morph_ttr, and text_ttr. Calculation scope (book, chapter, sentence, phrase, etc.), lower-case normalisation, and storage format.

page_notes.content: Note length-related bias inherent in TTR and typical ranges observed in the GNT.

pages.title: TF-IDF Features
pages.purpose: Reference for tfidf and tfidfns. Book-as-document model, stop-word handling, ×1,000,000 integer scaling, and provenance of the calculation pipeline.

page_notes.content: tfidfns excludes common function words (articles, prepositions, conjunctions, interjections).

pages.title: Cross-Reference Features
pages.purpose: Reference for betacode (word-level Beta Code encoding) and osis_id (book/chapter/verse identifiers following the OSIS standard).

page_notes.content: These features facilitate linking to external tools and corpora that use Beta Code or OSIS identifiers.

pages.title: Miscellaneous Features
pages.purpose: Reference for formaltag (GBI-style formal morphological tags), orig_order (word order from the XML Low Fat Tree source), penntree (experimental Penn Treebank-style syntax trees on sentence nodes), and num_words (word counts on structural nodes).

page_notes.content: penntree is explicitly marked experimental.

pages.title: Use Cases and Research Notebooks
pages.purpose: Overview of the Jupyter notebooks that demonstrate practical research workflows with the N1904addons features. Links to morphological analysis cases and statistical/syntactic cases.

page_notes.content: Notebooks serve both as documentation and as reproducible research environments.

pages.title: Morphological Analysis Use Cases
pages.purpose: Summary of notebooks that illustrate layered drill-down (mm → ms → md), exploration of known ambiguities, discovery of hidden lemmas, alternative lemma analyses, and gram_dif / regular-expression queries.

page_notes.content: These cases show how the Morpheus feature system makes morphological alternatives visible and queryable.

pages.title: Statistical and Syntactic Use Cases
pages.purpose: Summary of notebooks that combine ambiguity statistics with semantic selection, analyse phrase-function flip potential, study hapax legomena, and locate entropy hotspots (e.g., genealogies).

page_notes.content: Also covers utility notebooks for overview statistics on ambiguity and dataset footprint measurement.

pages.title: Text-Fabric Data Files Reference
pages.purpose: Technical notes on the .tf file format, metadata headers (valueType, description, node, provenance), and how feature files map to node identifiers. Distinguishes the standard tf/1.0.0/ set from the detailed_set.

page_notes.content: Useful for users who want to inspect or extend the feature files themselves.

pages.title: License, Citation and Provenance
pages.purpose: CC BY 4.0 licence statement, recommended BibTeX citation, Zenodo DOI, link to the related Research Master thesis, and brief provenance notes for the major feature families.

page_notes.content: Encourage proper attribution when the features are used in publications or downstream datasets.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.purpose: Definitions of key terms and abbreviations used throughout the repository and documentation: Beta Code, gram_dif, millibit, OSIS ID, PF flip, TTR, Morpheus analytic block, fieldmap, etc.

page_notes.content: Each entry should point to the relevant feature page or notebook where the concept is demonstrated.
